rules.sentence: The skin is examined for purplish lesions or lymph node enlargement that may signal the presence of Kaposi sarcoma.
Suspicious lesions on the skin or lymph nodes can be biopsied and sent to pathology for evaluation.
For a definitive diagnosis of Kaposi sarcoma, they must perform a biopsy or excision of the suspicious areas.
A pathologist examines the tissue under the microscope and looks for the characteristic features: a spindle cell vascular proliferation in the dermis.[20][3]
Immunohistochemistry positivity for LANA1 (a surrogate marker for HHV-8) helps to differentiate Kaposi sarcoma from similar lesions.
Skin involvement of Kaposi sarcoma is treated by local excision, liquid nitrogen, and injection of vincristine.[19][6]
Chemotherapy is a mainstay of treatment for endemic and systemic forms, in particular in children.[6][9]
